gpu.renderer: ANGLE (NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060/PCIe/SSE2, OpenGL ES 3.2 NVIDIA 610.57.04)

method: The 200 components are laid out as a grid (about square) first, as a real canvas is. Five seconds of real CDP wheel events (Input.dispatchMouseEvent, one every 16 ms, not waiting for each acknowledgement; about 300 are sent) while a Chromium trace (Tracing domain: devtools.timeline, frame, cc, viz) records. Frame time = the time between the presentations of consecutive frames that wanted an update (compositor PipelineReporter events inside the window). Counts of components on screen and un-culled come from geometry sampled every 100 ms without layout. Four runs: "pan" (30% zoom, selection centred, scrolling about 370 px back and forth: selection stays on screen), "pan+zoom" (the same with every twelfth event a Ctrl-wheel zoom step), "sweep+zoom" (30%, 25 px per event around a square of about 7,500 px of travel, with zoom steps: components are un-culled and rasterised continuously), "overview" (the sweep from 10% zoom). A floor run (a page that only moves a translate3d, own Chromium, same run) gives the compositor jitter of this machine at this moment. Pass, every run: raw p95 <= max(16.7, floor + 1) ms and at most 2% of frames >= 25 ms or dropped. CPU raster (--disable-gpu). The benchmark never gives the page a transform.
